evidence: MP: 'a difficult Bryan Burdo alpine rock climb' on the north face, no grade; AAJ 1988 (Burdo): 'In 1985 Bill Enger and I climbed Mount Persis' north face', no grade; a 2000 trip report: 'at least one Grade IV, super hard climbing route' on the north face.
note: No YDS number exists anywhere online after searches on the route name, the peak, Burdo/Enger and 1985; the only number is a commitment Grade IV, which is not a difficulty. Left ungraded. If a commitment value is wanted, the north-face route is reported as Grade IV.

evidence: Mountaineers rate the route Technical 3 to the summit (Technical 2 to Bathtub Lakes); a trip report describes ~900 ft of steep scrambling up Iodine Gulch on 'broken rock' and 'spots along the way with a bit of exposure'.
note: Mountaineers scramble rating T3 mapped to Class 3; the trip report corroborates the character but gives no class number.

evidence: FA account (1948): 40-degree debris slope, a crampon traverse across a '55-degree slope', then 'the first nearly vertical pitch of the chute' climbed by cutting holds, and knife-edge crevasse lips; route listings give Grade II-III with 50-60 degree snow and ice.
note: No published AI grade exists; 55-degree ice with a short near-vertical serac step maps to AI3. Conditions in an active icefall change yearly.

evidence: MP: Grade V, M5+ X (mixed), pins/screws/nuts/cams; a guide's analysis calls the ribs 'not very difficult' technically, with a reader reporting 'two pitches of 50-60 degree ice' to finish the West Rib direct.
note: The only published difficulty is MP's mixed grade M5+ X, which none of the three scales holds; AI3 is a mapping of 50-60 degree ice plus mixed ground, not a cited grade. The record's rock_grade 5.5 is not supported by any source found. Several ribs exist (West, Central, East) and the record does not say which.

evidence: Route page: a basic snow climb 'with some 3rd-4th class rock at the end'; a climber's log entry: at the 2nd major waterfall in the couloir, 'if dry, it presents an easy 4th / low 5th class ascent', and the summit is 'mostly 3rd class rock with a few 4th class moves'.
note: One party called the dry waterfall step 'easy 4th / low 5th'; in snow it is covered. Kept at the unroped ceiling, Class 4.

evidence: One guide service's North Face trip, which offers 'the seldom done Northeast Ridge, which requires additional ice climbing and complex alpine rock climbing', lists '5.7 rock climbing in mountain boots'; another groups the NE Ridge, SE Ridge and normal route as 'moderate rock climbing between 4th Class and 5.6'.
note: No source grades the NE Ridge alone. The normal and SE Ridge finishes top out at 5.6, so the 5.7 in the first guide most plausibly belongs to the NE Ridge option; that is an inference. The other guide's collective 4th-5.6 statement disagrees.

evidence: 2010 trip report: 'The step across under the summit rock on Mushroom was wet... We rapped off Beckey's two 1/4 inch bolts', no grade; The Mountaineer 1942: 'Mushroom Tower... via north face... Very difficult, one 6th class pitch.'
note: No modern route page or number found (MP lists no routes on Mushroom Tower). '6th class' in 1942 meant an aid pitch, presumably at the bolted summit block. 5.5 is the top of the record's own 5.4/5.5 split.
identity: The 1942 first ascent went 'via north face', while this record is titled South Side and credits that ascent to it.

evidence: Traverse report: 'a key heather ramp on Mutchler's NE Ridge that took me up on relatively easy ground to the flat summit plateau', then 400 ft to the summit; the Snowking approach this route climbs first is a Class 3 scramble.
note: Mutchler itself is easy ground (Class 2); the Class 3 crux is the Snowking/Kindy Ridge portion the record says the route climbs first. The Mutchler Glacier can be firm late season.

evidence: Peak page: 'the broad Northwest Couloir of North Gardner offers a pretty easy and direct route to the summit'; a Cedar Creek ascent report describes snow from 4,000 ft covering brush and talus to the summit.
note: No class number for this line exists online. Class 3 rests on the record's own talus-ridge finish plus its report of hard, icy snow needing committing crampon work (firm steep snow mapped to Class 3); on soft snow it would be Class 2. Searched SP, MP, NWMJ, WTA, Peakbagger.

evidence: The 1929 Chute-Kaartinen line is the North Face Route of the North Peak, 'Grade III, Class 5.6'; a 2020 report: 'the North Face has ended up with a sandbagged 5.6'; a 2016 report climbs the NE Rib, then 'thick jungle climbing for three rope lengths' to the great bowl and the north rib.
note: Two sources agree on 5.6 (one party off-route called a brushy pitch 5.7). It is notoriously sandbagged by wet moss and vertical brush. The summer route has no graded ice, so the record's WI3- does not belong to it.
identity: This is the North Face Route of Index's North Peak (Chute and Kaartinen, 1929), which starts up the NE Rib; no separate 'Northeast Buttress' route is documented anywhere.

evidence: Peak page: from Lyman Lake 'cross-country through open meadows and then talus/scree (Class 2) on south side', 'scrambling is required to reach the summit'; a trip report scrambles a gully and the SW ridge to the top with no harder moves reported.

fix.rock_grade: Class 2 (talus and scree; easy summit scramble)

note: No source anywhere gives the Class 3-4 '3.5' summit step in the record. That description matches neighbouring Cloudy Peak, whose summit block reports call Class 3-4, and looks borrowed from it.

evidence: Peak page: 'a 2- or 3-pitch easy/moderate class 5 route on the east side'; guide service: 'Two pitches of mid-fifth class climbing' up the east ridge from the Le Conte Glacier.
note: Two independent sources agree on mid-fifth, but neither gives a number; 'mid-fifth' mapped to 5.5.

evidence: 1952 FA account: 500 ft of difficult rock to the Pernod-Chianti notch, pitons, a bolt-protected pendulum and bolts near the summit; MP lists only the Direct West Face (5.10+) and South Face (5.9 A0), not this line.
note: No modern free grade for the notch route found online. 5.7 is the top of the record's 5.5-5.7. The easiest routes on the neighbouring Wine Spires are Grade II (Chianti N Face II 5.6, Chablis E Face II 5.6), so the record's commitment III-IV looks high, but nothing route-specific confirms it.

evidence: MP: Luna Glacier, 'Easy 5th', 3 pitches, Steep Snow, M1c; Wikipedia: the normal Southwest Route is Class 4; a trip report up the SW pocket glacier: bergschrund, 'moderately steep snow finger', 'Class 2-3 scrambling', an exposed summit ridge where they fixed 'a hand line'.
note: Easy 5th with no cited number mapped to 5.0 per the brief. The record's breakdown '5.2-5.4' has no source. A '50 ft 5.5 corner with 3 fixed pitons' that turns up in searches belongs to Mount Challenger, not Phantom.
